title: Position and Displacement on an Axis
short: Pick an origin and a positive direction; displacement Δx = x_final − x_initial carries a sign.
trouble: Students compute displacement as the total distance traveled, ignoring a change of direction.

blocks.html: In Distance and Displacement you met the difference between how far you went and where you ended up. To work with numbers, physicists put the motion on an axis: pick an origin ($x = 0$) and a positive direction. Then every position is a signed number, like the integers in Subtracting Integers.

Displacement is final position minus initial position: $\Delta x = x_f - x_i$. Its sign tells the direction: positive means it ended up on the $+x$ side of where it started, negative means the $-x$ side.

Subtraction measures the gap between two numbers on a number line, including which way you step to get from the first to the second. Going from $x = 2$ to $x = 7$ is a step of $+5$; going from $7$ back to $2$ is a step of $-5$. Displacement is exactly that step, for the whole trip at once, so it ignores everything that happened in between.

blocks.name: ph-motion

opts.task: Press Play. Watch the distance keep growing while the displacement grows, shrinks and turns negative.

blocks.cap: The cart starts at x = 4 m, rolls right, stops and comes back past where it started. The odometer adds every meter; the displacement only compares the end with the start.

blocks.title: A move to the left
blocks.q: A cart starts at $x = 3\ \text{m}$ and stops at $x = -5\ \text{m}$. Find its displacement.
steps: $\Delta x = -8\ \text{m}$. The minus sign says it moved 8 m in the $-x$ direction.

blocks.title: Out and back
blocks.q: A runner goes from $x = 10\ \text{m}$ to $x = 70\ \text{m}$, then turns and jogs back to $x = 40\ \text{m}$. Find the displacement and the distance.
steps: Displacement uses only the ends: $\Delta x = 40 - 10 = 30\ \text{m}$.
Distance adds the length of every leg: $60\ \text{m}$ out and $30\ \text{m}$ back.

blocks.html: Using the total distance as the displacement. When the motion changes direction, the two differ: the runner above traveled 90 m but is only 30 m from the start. Check: displacement can be negative or zero; distance never can. If an object ends where it began, its displacement is zero however far it went.
